Godan verb; in 役に立つ, means 'to be useful'.

examples.text: ここに立ってください。
この経験はきっと役に立ちます。
examples.trans: This experience will surely be useful.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: 誠実な政治を取り戻し、日本を救うためには何が必要か！
examples.trans: What is needed to restore honest politics and save Japan!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 誠実な政治を取り戻し、日本を救うためには何が必要か！
examples.trans: What is needed to restore honest politics and save Japan!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: 誠実な政治を取り戻し、日本を救うためには何が必要か！
examples.trans: What is needed to restore honest politics and save Japan!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Read にほん (Nihon) or にっぽん (Nippon).

examples.text: 日本の文化が好きです。
助けたい人間も救えるんじゃないか？
examples.trans: And couldn't you also rescue the person you want to save?

examples.text: 監督を救うには大金が必要なんだ。俺だけじゃ集めらんない。
examples.trans: Rescuing the director takes huge money. I cannot raise it on my own.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Humble noun form of 待たせる, used in apologies like お待たせしました.

examples.text: 大変お待たせいたしました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for waiting.

examples.text: お待たせしてすみません。

meanings.note: Humble (kenjougo) equivalent of する, used in polite business and apologetic expressions.

examples.text: すぐにご連絡いたします。
examples.trans: I will contact you right away.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。
しかたがないだろ。世の中興味ねえよ。
examples.trans: Nothing can be done. The public does not care.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: そんなことしたら世の中がめちゃくちゃになりますよ！
examples.trans: If you aired things like that on television, society would fall apart!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Polite/honorific term for someone else's wife or the lady of the house.

examples.text: 奥様によろしくお伝えください。
examples.trans: Please give my regards to your wife.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Noun.

examples.text: 時代が変わりましたね。

meanings.note: Colloquial quotative/emphatic particle expressing surprise or dismissal.

examples.text: そんなことなんて知らない。
examples.trans: I don't know anything like that.

examples.text: 嘘だなんて信じられない。
examples.trans: I can't believe it's a lie.

meanings.note: Godan verb; in ～ということ, means 'the fact that...' or 'meaning that...'.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。
役者の質が低くないか？大丈夫なんだろうな？
examples.trans: Isn't the quality of the actors a bit low? Are you sure about them?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Polite/honorific plural pronoun for addressing an audience or group.

examples.text: こんにちは、お元気ですか。
こんにちは、いい天気ですね。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
